title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: federated connectors can create, update and delete in third-party systems
summary: Hold: Copilot Chat access alone does not meet the published licensing requirements, and the individual-tool blocking row links to a nonexistent page and describes server blocking instead. The staged-rollout path omits Edit, and the prose conflicts with the controls table about tool blocking.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.where: front matter: releasePhase
claims.claim: The release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.quote: "platforms": ["Desktop", "Web"]

claims.quote: "targetDate": "October CY2026"

claims.where: What's changing: opening paragraph
claims.claim: Federated connectors use Model Context Protocol to query third-party data in real time.
claims.quote: Federated connectors use MCP to access data in real time, so Copilot can retrieve up-to-date information directly from external systems.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Federated connectors do not index external data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: No data is indexed into Microsoft 365. Copilot sends the connector the information it needs to complete the action and returns the outcome to the user.

claims.where: What's changing: Until October 2026
claims.claim: Federated connectors were read-only before the October 2026 write-actions change.
claims.quote:
Write actions will be available starting early October 2026.

- Federated connectors are read-only; they can search and fetch content but can't write data back.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing: opening paragraph
claims.claim: The update unblocks connector-provided create, update and delete tools in Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: With this update, the connector tools that create, update, and delete content in those services are unblocked in Copilot Chat, so users can complete work without leaving Copilot.

claims.where: What's changing: escalation email, CRM record and comment examples
claims.claim: Documented write-action examples include turning an escalation email into an issue, updating a CRM record and commenting on a ticket.
claims.quote: For example, a user can turn an escalation email into an issue in a project-tracking tool, update a record in a customer relationship management (CRM) system, or add a comment to a ticket directly from Copilot Chat.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure and Security & identity
claims.claim: Actions use the user's account and can change only what that user is permitted to change in the source system.
claims.quote: Actions run in the third-party service on behalf of the user and are limited by that user's permissions. Copilot can change only what the user is already permitted to change in the source system.

claims.where: summary; What's changing: Needs approval
claims.claim: Write, update and delete tools initially default to Needs approval.
claims.quote: Write, update, and delete tools default to **Needs approval**, which means Copilot asks for confirmation each time.
claims.fix: Attribute the detailed reusable-approval behaviour to Learn and report that the roadmap instead says every create, update or delete action requires explicit confirmation. Qualify the summary as initial approval rather than implying confirmation on every invocation.

claims.where: What's changing: confirmation card; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Users can expand a confirmation card to inspect the action parameters before approving.
claims.quote: Users can expand the card to review the action parameters before approving it.

claims.where: What's changing: nothing is transmitted until the user responds
claims.claim: While an action awaits confirmation, nothing is sent to the connected system until the user responds.
claims.quote: While an action is awaiting confirmation, nothing is sent to the connected system until the user responds.

claims.where: What's changing: Allow once; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Allow once approves the current action and leaves confirmation required for the next use of the tool.
claims.quote: **Allow once** | Runs the action now. Copilot asks again the next time it wants to use the tool.

claims.where: What's changing: Allow for conversation
claims.claim: Allow for conversation suppresses further confirmation for that individual tool during the current conversation.
claims.quote: **Allow for conversation** | Runs the action and doesn't ask again for this tool for the rest of the current conversation.

claims.where: What's changing: Always allow; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Always allow suppresses confirmation for the individual tool until the user changes its setting or the publisher changes the tool.
claims.quote: **Always allow** | Runs the action and doesn't ask again for this tool until the user changes the setting or the publisher changes the tool.

claims.where: What's changing: Cancel; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Cancel declines the action and leaves the connected system unchanged.
claims.quote: **Cancel** | Declines the action. Nothing is changed in the connected system.

claims.where: What's changing: revocable in Settings > Sources
claims.claim: Users can review or reset approval permissions through Copilot Settings > Sources by selecting the connector.
claims.quote: Users can review or reset tool permissions in Copilot by going to **Settings** > **Sources** and selecting the connector.

claims.where: What's changing: publisher adds or changes a write tool
claims.claim: A newly added or changed write-capable tool is set to Needs approval.
claims.quote: If a connector publisher adds a new write-capable tool or changes an existing one, the tool is set to **Needs approval** by default.

claims.where: summary; What's changing: admin tool lists; Governance controls: connector details pane
claims.claim: Administrators can view each connector's read and write/delete tools in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Admins can view each connector's read and write/delete tools in the Microsoft 365 admin center and disable connectors that don't meet their organization's policies.
claims.fix: Report both sources: the roadmap says admins can view tools, but Learn labels this Coming soon and says it is not available for all connectors. Explain that supported connectors require third-party sign-in in Tools > All tools, that the list reflects that account's permissions, and give the Copilot Settings > Sources > connector > Write/Delete tools fallback.

claims.where: What's changing: disable connectors; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Administrators can disable individual federated connectors at tenant level.
claims.quote: Enable or disable connectors at the tenant level.

claims.where: What's changing: supported experiences; Scope
claims.claim: Federated connectors support Copilot Chat, agents, Cowork and Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook.
claims.quote:
Microsoft 365 Copilot supports federated Copilot connectors in the following experiences:

- Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat
- Agents
- Cowork
- Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook
- Researcher agent

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Scope
claims.claim: The Researcher agent remains read-only and does not support write, update or delete actions.
claims.quote: The Researcher agent doesn't support write, update, or delete actions. Federated Copilot connectors remain read-only in this experience.

claims.where: What's changing: Microsoft-published default connectors
claims.claim: Microsoft's default federated connectors appear as Ready in the admin center connection list.
claims.quote: Default federated connectors are provided by Microsoft and appear as **Ready** in your connections list in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Open questions: admin-published templates
claims.claim: Admin-published federated connector templates currently support read-only tools only.
claims.quote: Make sure the MCP server exposes at least one tool annotated as read-only. Admin-published FCCs currently support read-only tools only.

claims.where: Why it matters: first time
claims.claim: This is the first time Microsoft 365 Copilot itself, rather than a custom agent, can change third-party data.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft 365 Copilot" "first time" "third-party" "write". Read federated-connectors-overview, connectors/overview, and release-notes search excerpts; none establishes this first across all Copilot mechanisms.
claims.fix: Replace the historical superlative with 'Federated connectors now let Microsoft 365 Copilot change data in connected third-party systems.'

claims.where: Why it matters: Purview audit; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout and After rollout
claims.claim: Administrators can audit federated connector activity in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: Can read data and, where a connector provides the tools, create, update, or delete data with the user's approval. Admins can audit activity in Microsoft Purview.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Write tools belong to the enabled connector and do not require a separate administrator enablement.
claims.quote: Write, update, and delete tools are part of the connector and aren't enabled separately.

claims.where: Why it matters: export Customer Data; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Write actions export Customer Data from the Copilot workflow to the connected third-party system.
claims.quote: These actions export Customer Data to the connected system to create, update, delete, or otherwise modify data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Federated connector access uses OAuth authentication.
claims.quote: OAuth 2.0 and encrypted communication ensure secure access and authentication.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity, static egress
claims.claim: An MCP server that restricts inbound source IP addresses needs to allow Microsoft's static egress IP addresses for Copilot MCP requests.
claims.quote: If your MCP server restricts incoming traffic by source IP address, configure its firewall to allow the static egress IP addresses used by Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Copilot dynamically selects relevant connector tools at runtime.
claims.quote: When appropriate, Microsoft 365 Copilot dynamically selects relevant tools to retrieve information or perform an action.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented a tenant-wide administrator setting that forces Needs approval or overrides Always allow for these write tools.
claims.quote: Searched: "federated connectors" "always require approval" administrator; "federated connectors" "approval" "admin" "audit". Opened federated-connectors-overview, manage-federated-connectors and agent-settings; no such override documented.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, no per-tool admin switch; controls[3]
claims.claim: There is no per-tool administrator switch.
claims.quote: **Tools block / unblock** | **Agents** > **Tools** | Tool-level and connector-level blocking.
claims.fix: Remove the blanket absence claim and reconcile it with controls[3]. Say write tools are not enabled separately, while Microsoft documents tool-level blocking for supported Agent 365 MCP servers only; do not promise it covers every federated connector. Cite the supported-server qualifications at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model
claims.claim: Connector grounding is included for appropriately licensed Microsoft 365 Copilot users.
claims.quote: If your organization has Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, connector grounding in Copilot is included, and no extra charges apply.
claims.fix: Keep licensing.model included, add this prerequisites URL to sources, and name the required Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence or Microsoft 365 E7 explicitly.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: first bullet
claims.claim: Copilot Chat entitlements alone qualify a user for included access to federated connectors.
claims.quote: Federated Copilot connectors are available only to tenants and users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license (or Microsoft 365 E7). They aren't supported with Copilot Studio licenses or Microsoft 365 Copilot pay-as-you-go.
claims.fix: Replace the licensing notes and first licensing bullet with 'Federated connectors require a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence for every user, or Microsoft 365 E7. Copilot Chat access alone and Copilot pay-as-you-go do not qualify. Connector grounding is included for qualifying users.' Cite this prerequisites page.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: third-party licence
claims.claim: Third-party services may impose their own licensing obligations.
claims.quote: As the data controller, you're solely and exclusively responsible for: a) the Connector Functionality; and b) using the Microsoft 365 Copilot connector in compliance with any third-party rights, licenses, and obligations.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/terms-of-use to sources for the third-party licensing qualification.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: third-party API calls; rationale: cost
claims.claim: External APIs and independently operated services may introduce costs beyond the connector entitlement.
claims.quote: Packaging a capability doesn't remove the cost of operating its dependencies. Include hosting, model usage, storage, networking, credentials, monitoring, and support for any remote MCP servers, APIs, or other services your plugin uses.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/cost-considerations and frame third-party API charges as provider-specific costs to check, not a universal connector charge.

claims.where: Scope: users and staged rollout; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Connector access is limited to eligible users allowed by tenant access settings and the connector's staged audience who connect their own source account.
claims.quote:
The user is included in **User access**.
- The user is included in the connector's staged rollout.
- The user has a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.where: Scope: Government cloud availability not stated
claims.claim: The roadmap record does not state government cloud availability.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: Connector enable, disable and staging controls are in Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Your connections for the selected connector.
claims.quote: **Enable / Disable** | **Copilot** > **Connectors** > **Your connections** | Turns an individual connector on or pauses it without removing configuration.

claims.claim: No equivalent API or PowerShell control is documented for federated connector enablement and disablement.
claims.quote: Searched: "federated connectors" "enable" "disable" "PowerShell" "API". Opened manage-federated-connectors and federated-connectors-overview; read set-up-custom-federated-connectors management excerpts. No equivalent command found.

claims.where: controls[1].ui and note; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access controls connector availability by Microsoft, organisational or external publisher type, including future connectors.
claims.quote: **Agent and plugin access** | **Agents** > **Settings** > **Agent and plugin access** | Allows or blocks connectors in bulk by publisher type, including future connectors.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: automation absence
claims.claim: No equivalent API or PowerShell control is documented for Agent and plugin access publisher-type settings.
claims.quote: Searched: "Agent and plugin access" "User access" "PowerShell" "Graph". Opened agent-settings, manage-federated-connectors and manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers under microsoft-agent-365/admin; no equivalent publisher-type command found.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls: third table row
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access sets which users or groups may use agents and plugins, including connectors.
claims.quote: Select **Agents** > **Settings** > **User access** to manage your organization's agents and plugins.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls: automation absence
claims.claim: No equivalent API or PowerShell command is documented for the Agents settings User access control.
claims.quote: Searched: "Agent and plugin access" "User access" "PowerShell" "Graph". Opened agent-settings and manage-federated-connectors; results on app-role assignments and agent identities do not document this User access setting.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; Governance controls: Blocking an individual tool
claims.claim: Agents > Tools > Registry > tool > Block blocks an individual connector tool, as documented at the cited microsoft-365/copilot URL.
claims.quote: Select the **Tools** tab. The list shows every tool the server exposes, along with its description and an **Enabled** or **Disabled** toggle.
claims.fix: The cited https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers returns HTTP 404. Replace it with this Agent 365 page. For individual tools use Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Tools > tool toggle > Save, not the server's Block button. State that granular control is rolling out only for supported registered MCP servers, with no blanket applicability to every federated connector; alternatively remove this row and describe the qualified general control in notes.

claims.where: controls[3].api; Governance controls: automation absence
claims.claim: No equivalent API or PowerShell command is documented for the individual-tool blocking control described in the row.
claims.quote: Searched: "MCP" "tool" "block" "Graph" "PowerShell" "Agent 365". Opened microsoft-agent-365/admin/manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers; read CLI and Azure gateway excerpts. No equivalent individual-tool command for this connector control found.

claims.where: controls[4].ui; Governance controls: Who is in a staged rollout
claims.claim: The cited Modify staged rollout instructions end at Your connections > connector > Staged rollout.
claims.quote:
In the **Staged Rollout** column, next to **Staged**, choose **Edit**.
4. Add or remove users and groups from the staged rollout, and choose **Save**.
claims.fix: Change controls[4].ui.path and the rendered row to 'Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections > connector > Staged Rollout > Edit'. The existing cited instructions require Edit to open the audience editor.

claims.where: controls[4].api; Governance controls: automation absence
claims.claim: No equivalent API or PowerShell command is documented for connector staged-rollout audience configuration.
claims.quote: Searched: "staged rollout" "connectors" "Graph" "API"; "federated connectors" "PowerShell" "Graph" "staged". Opened staged-rollout and manage-federated-connectors; read custom connector management excerpts. No equivalent staging command found.

claims.where: Governance controls: Users approve write actions per connector in Copilot Chat settings
claims.claim: Users manage their own connector write-tool approval settings in Copilot Chat, rather than through an administrator approval control.
claims.quote: **Always allow** and **Allow for conversation** apply to the individual tool, not to the whole connector. Users can decide which tools to allow.
claims.fix: Replace 'Users approve write actions per connector' with 'Users manage individual tool approvals under Settings > Sources > connector > Tools > Write/Delete tools; reusable approvals apply to a tool, not the whole connector.'

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The write-capability change is on for existing enabled connectors without a separate administrator switch.
claims.quote: Write, update, and delete tools are part of the connector and aren't enabled separately.

claims.where: front matter: cost; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Connector grounding has no extra Microsoft charge for users who already hold the qualifying Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.quote: If your organization has Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, connector grounding in Copilot is included, and no extra charges apply.
claims.fix: Cite the prerequisites page and scope the None rationale to the incremental connector-grounding charge for already licensed users. Do not equate inclusion with free Copilot Chat eligibility or with every supported host experience being unmetered.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Confirm Purview audit; Governance controls: table
claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to check Purview auditing but the controls table has no audit row.
claims.quote: Confirm Purview audit is capturing connector actions for the pilot. / The table lists connector availability, publisher access, User access, tool blocking and staged rollout, but no audit control.
claims.fix: Add a row governing review of connector activity in Microsoft Purview. Read and cite the exact audit-search UI/API instructions before supplying paths or commands; retain the feature overview as evidence that auditing applies to federated connectors.

claims.where: Risk assessment: no approval override; Governance controls: table
claims.claim: The text reports a missing tenant-wide approval override without representing that control gap in the table.
claims.quote: There is no admin control described for forcing Needs approval tenant-wide. / No controls row records a tenant-wide approval-default override.
claims.fix: Add a 'Tenant-wide requirement to approve write actions' control row with ui and api null and a note that no administrator override is documented as of November 2026.

claims.where: Open questions: DLP inspection of write payloads
claims.claim: Whether Copilot-location DLP can inspect these federated write payloads remains undocumented in the feature guidance.
claims.quote: Searched: "federated connectors" "DLP" "government". Opened federated-connectors-overview and read returned custom-connector FAQ and Power Platform data-policy excerpts; none confirms Copilot-location DLP inspection of these write payloads.
